metaDescription: Six kitchen trash cans compared on touchless sensors, slim footprints, removable liners and soft-close pedals, so you can match a bin to your cooking habits.
introParagraphs: A kitchen bin takes more abuse than any other can in the house. It gets raw scraps, wet coffee grounds, greasy packaging and a dozen trips a day, and it sits where everyone can see it. The right choice depends less on brand and more on how your kitchen is laid out and how you handle waste while cooking.

The six picks below split into clear camps. The BestOffice is a touchless 13-gallon bin that runs on four C batteries, the Glad Slim is a narrow 12-gallon steel bin for tight rooms, and the PayLessHere has a removable inner bucket. The KdbK and SONGMICS are 13-gallon steel pedal bins with soft-close lids, and the Glad Premium is a plastic 13-gallon with a stainless pedal.

We evaluated them on the listing specs and buyer feedback themes, thinking about the real kitchen moments: hands covered in dough, a full bag to lift out, a narrow gap beside the fridge. Read on to see which design matches your routine.

products.name: KdbK 13 Gallon Stainless Steel Kitchen Trash Can
products.description:
For a typical family kitchen, the KdbK covers the basics without any gimmicks. The 13-gallon size matches standard kitchen liners, the brushed stainless surface resists fingerprints, and the pedal frees both hands while you scrape a cutting board. Twenty bags in the box mean you can start using it the day it arrives.

The lid mechanism is a bi-force damper, which pulls the lid shut gently whether you released the pedal or lowered it by hand. That detail matters in a kitchen that opens onto a dining area, because a slamming lid is the sound everyone notices after dinner. The ABS parts mentioned in the listing help keep the mechanism light.

It is not the slimmest bin or the smartest. Next to the Glad Slim, it takes more floor space, and next to the BestOffice, it needs a foot rather than a sensor. In day-to-day cooking, though, a plain pedal that closes quietly is hard to beat, and it sidesteps the batteries that a touchless bin needs.
products.bestFor: Family kitchens that want a quiet, simple steel pedal can.
pros: Damper closes the lid without a slam
Starter bags come in the box
No batteries or electronics to maintain
cons: Larger footprint than a slim bin
Pedal is the likely wear point

products.name: BestOffice 13 Gallon Touchless Stainless Steel Trash Can
products.description:
Anyone who has opened a bin with flour-coated hands will understand the appeal of a sensor lid. The BestOffice opens and closes on its own when you wave a hand or a plate over it, so you never touch the surface. The body is stainless steel with a fingerprint-resistant finish, and the oval shape with a sloping lid is meant to suit modern kitchens.

Power comes from four C batteries, which are not included, and the listing supports 40,000 or more openings. Alkaline cells are the type suggested, so factor in the ongoing cost and the occasional battery swap. When the cells run low, the lid behavior can slow or stop, which is the main annoyance with any sensor can.

Compared with the KdbK, you swap a mechanical pedal for electronics, which is a plus for convenience and a minus for simplicity. Compared with the PayLessHere, it has no removable bucket. If you have limited mobility in your feet or simply hate touching a lid, this is the clear choice. If you want zero maintenance, a pedal can wins.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want to open the bin without touching anything.
pros: Sensor lid opens and closes by itself
Oval shape with sloping lid saves space
cons: Needs four C batteries, not included
Sensor can misfire near the bin
More parts to fail than a pedal

products.name: Glad 12 Gallon Slim Stainless Steel Trash Can
products.description:
Many kitchens have one awkward gap beside a fridge or a pantry door, and the Glad Slim is made for it. Its narrow profile slips into tight spaces, yet it still holds 12 gallons, which the listing equates to 45 liters. The body is a heavy-duty rectangular stainless steel with a fingerprint-resistant finish.

A soft-close lid and a step pedal handle daily use, and bag rings keep the liner from sliding inside. The lid is formulated with Clorox protection meant to trap odors and provide an airtight seal. That combination of narrow body and sealed lid fits small kitchens that cannot spare floor space but still deal with the usual cooking smells.

The cost of slimness is a little less volume than the 13-gallon bins, so you may empty it slightly more often. It also needs liners sized for its narrow shape, which are not always the same as standard bags. Compared with the Glad Premium, the Slim is steel rather than plastic, and compared with the KdbK, it trades width for a bit of capacity. For tight corners, it is the standout.
products.bestFor: Small kitchens with a narrow gap for the bin.
pros: Bag rings hold the liner in place
cons: Narrow liner shape may need matching bags

products.name: PayLessHere 13 Gallon Steel Trash Can with Inner Bucket
products.description:
The removable inner bucket is the reason to consider the PayLessHere. When a bag leaks or a spill needs a proper rinse, you can lift the bucket out, take it to the sink and wash it, instead of tipping a whole steel bin on its side. That one feature solves the cleaning problem that most steel pedal cans ignore.

The outer body is stainless steel that the listing says wipes clean with a damp cloth and resists bacteria and germs. A step pedal opens the lid and a soft-close mechanism keeps it from slamming. The 13-gallon size fits standard kitchen liners, and the listing positions it as a bin to keep beside the kitchen table.

It does not list a fingerprint-resistant finish the way the KdbK and BestOffice do, so smudges may show. There is also no odor filter like the one on the SIMPLI-MAGIC. If your priority is a bin that can be rinsed out regularly, and you cook often with wet scraps, this is the pick. If you want a simple lid with the best finish, choose the KdbK.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want to lift out and rinse the inner bucket.
pros: Removable inner bucket rinses at the sink
cons: No odor filter or treated lid
Extra part to store when washing

products.name: Glad Premium 13 Gallon Plastic Step Trash Can
products.description:
The Glad Premium is the lighter, plainer option for people who do not need a steel look. The rectangular matte body keeps a classic shape that slides against a wall, and the listing says the lid is formulated with Clorox Odor Protection. The pedal has been redesigned with a stainless steel construction for durability.

Plastic keeps the weight down, which is useful on emptying day when you lift the full bin out to the curb. It will not dent from a bump, though it can scratch. A rectangular shape wastes less floor than a round bin of similar capacity.

The tradeoff is feel and finish. The Glad Premium does not offer a soft-close damper in its listing, so the lid drops with a firmer motion than on the KdbK or SONGMICS. Compared with the Glad Slim, it is wider but cheaper in materials, and compared with the PayLessHere, it has no inner bucket. For a budget-minded kitchen where simplicity wins, it is a reasonable all-rounder.
products.bestFor: Kitchens that want a light plastic can with an odor-treated lid.
pros: Light plastic body is easy to carry out
cons: Less premium than a steel bin

products.name: SONGMICS 13 Gallon Fluted Stainless Steel Trash Can
products.description:
The SONGMICS looks like part of the kitchen rather than a bin hidden in a corner. Its fluted exterior catches the light, and the metallic-enhanced powder coating over premium stainless steel gives it a shimmering surface that the listing describes as changing with the angle. The coating is meant to resist wear.

Useful features back up the styling. You can step on the pedal for hands-free use or lift the lid by hand to 90 degrees to keep it open while you clear leftovers. When the lid closes, it does so softly, so there is no clang in an open-plan room.

The flutes collect crumbs and splashes more than a flat drum does, so wiping takes a little longer. Against the KdbK, you gain a more decorative look and a hold-open lid, but you lose the included bags. Compared with the BestOffice, you keep the simplicity of a pedal. For a kitchen where the can is always on display, it earns its place.
products.bestFor: Open kitchens where the bin is part of the room.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The way a lid opens determines how comfortable the can is with messy hands. The KdbK, PayLessHere, Glad Slim and SONGMICS use foot pedals, the BestOffice uses a sensor lid, and the Glad Premium uses a step pedal. Sensor lids need four C batteries on the BestOffice, so budget for that. If you cook a lot, test how far the pedal travels and how firm it feels. A stiff pedal becomes irritating when you use it dozens of times a day.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Width and depth of the gap
buyingCriteria.explanation: Kitchen gaps are rarely generous. The Glad Slim is a narrow 12-gallon bin built for tight spaces, while the 13-gallon KdbK and SONGMICS take more width. Measure the opening, then add room for the lid to swing. A bin that blocks a drawer or a dishwasher door will be an everyday annoyance.

Thirteen gallons suits most kitchens and fits standard liners, while 12 gallons on the Glad Slim is slightly smaller. A bigger can lets you wait longer between trips but also lets food waste sit. Consider your household size and how often you cook from scratch. A small kitchen with two people can stay on the smaller side.

Kitchen cans see leaks, so cleanability matters. The PayLessHere has a removable inner bucket that lifts out for rinsing, which is a major advantage over a fixed steel interior. Other bins need a wipe-down in place or a tilt to the sink. Look for smooth interiors, minimal crevices and a bag ring that keeps liners out of the corners.

The Glad Premium and Glad Slim use lids formulated with Clorox odor protection, while the KdbK relies on a quiet-close lid and stainless body. A tighter seal slows odors from leaking into the room but cannot beat an overdue bag. Empty food waste regularly, particularly after cooking meat or fish, and wipe the rim of the bin when it gets greasy. Greasy residue on the rim is what makes a closed lid smell, so a quick wipe each week does more than most add-on features.

Kitchens see fingerprints and splashes. The KdbK and BestOffice list fingerprint-resistant finishes, and the Glad Slim also lists a fingerprint-resistant steel surface. The SONGMICS powder coating is built to resist wear but its flutes hold dirt. Pick a finish that matches how often you are willing to wipe.

howWeEvaluated.title: Everyday kitchen use
howWeEvaluated.description: We pictured how each bin behaves when your hands are full or dirty. The BestOffice opens by sensor, the pedal models open with a foot, and we noted which listings describe soft-close or fingerprint-resistant features for the daily grind.

howWeEvaluated.title: Footprint fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared shapes and sizes. The Glad Slim is narrow at 12 gallons, while the KdbK, SONGMICS, PayLessHere, BestOffice and Glad Premium hold 13 gallons. The shape decides whether a can fits into a tight gap beside a fridge.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning and upkeep
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at inner design and surface finish. The PayLessHere stands out for its removable inner bucket, and the KdbK and BestOffice for anti-fingerprint steel. We also noted the battery upkeep that comes with the BestOffice sensor.

howWeEvaluated.title: Odor and seal
howWeEvaluated.description: We recorded which cans mention treated lids or seals, including the Clorox protection on both Glad cans. We treated odor features as helpful but not magic.

howWeEvaluated.title: Placement in the lineup
howWeEvaluated.description: We positioned the picks against each other: the KdbK as the balanced steel can, the BestOffice for touchless use, the Glad Slim for narrow spaces, the PayLessHere for easy rinsing, the Glad Premium for lightness and the SONGMICS for styling.

cards.label: Pedal cans
cards.text: The KdbK, SONGMICS, PayLessHere, Glad Slim and Glad Premium open with a foot press. They need no batteries, are simple to repair and work every time. They require you to stand in front of the bin and use a foot, which may be awkward for some. Choose a pedal if you want reliability and low upkeep.

cards.label: Touchless cans
cards.text: The BestOffice opens with a sensor and runs on four C batteries. It spares your foot and keeps the lid clean, but it can misfire and depends on fresh cells. Choose touchless if foot pedals are uncomfortable or if you hate touching any lid.

faq.q: What is the best size for a kitchen trash can?
faq.a: Thirteen gallons is the common choice and matches standard kitchen bags. It suits most families and keeps trips to the curb reasonable. If your kitchen is tight, the 12-gallon Glad Slim is a close alternative with a narrower body.

faq.q: Is a touchless kitchen trash can worth it?
faq.a: It depends on how you cook. The BestOffice keeps your hands off the lid, which is handy with sticky or raw food on your fingers. The cost is four C batteries and the chance of sensor hiccups, so if you want zero upkeep, a pedal can is simpler.

faq.q: How do I stop a kitchen bin from smelling?
faq.a: Empty food waste often, especially after cooking meat or fish. Use a bin with a tight lid, such as the Glad cans with Clorox odor protection, and rinse the inside when something leaks. A lid cannot make up for a bag that sits for days.

faq.q: Why does a removable inner bucket matter?
faq.a: It lets you wash the part that actually touches the trash without tipping a heavy steel bin. The PayLessHere has this feature. If your kitchen produces wet scraps, it can make cleanup much easier.

faq.q: Will a stainless steel bin show fingerprints?
faq.a: Many do, but several listings here describe fingerprint-resistant finishes, including the KdbK, BestOffice and Glad Slim. Wipe with a soft cloth in the direction of the grain. Fluted designs like the SONGMICS need a little extra care in the grooves.

faq.q: How do I keep the bag from slipping inside?
faq.a: Choose a bin with bag rings, such as the Glad Slim, and fold the bag edge over the rim. Match the bag size to the bin. A bag that is too small will pull down into the can.

faq.q: Can a pedal can be hard to use?
faq.a: Pedals need a little foot pressure and balance, which some people find tiring over many uses. If so, a touchless bin like the BestOffice may be more comfortable. An occupational therapist can offer advice if you have specific mobility concerns.
